# linearctl issue

<!-- Generated by scripts/skill-docs.py from --help; do not edit. -->

## linearctl issue archive

```
Archive an issue. An issue already archived is changed: false.
Changes things: pass --dry-run to preview, --yes to apply.

Usage:
  linearctl issue archive ISSUE [flags]

Examples:
  linearctl issue archive ENG-123 --dry-run
  linearctl issue archive ENG-123 --yes --json

Flags:
      --dry-run   show what would change; change nothing
  -h, --help      help for archive
      --yes       apply the change
```

## linearctl issue create

```
Create an issue in a team. Names (state, label, project, assignee email) are
resolved to ids first; --dry-run prints the exact input it would send.

--yes requires --id, a UUID you choose, so a rerun can never create a second
issue: if one with that id exists, it is returned with changed: false.
--dry-run without --id generates one and prints it as id; pass it to --yes.
Changes things: pass --dry-run to preview, --yes to apply.

Usage:
  linearctl issue create [flags]

Examples:
  linearctl issue create --team ENG --title "Fix login timeout" --label bug --dry-run --json
  linearctl issue create --team ENG --title "Fix login timeout" --label bug --yes --id 0b6c…
  linearctl issue create --json-input issue.json --id 0b6c… --yes

Flags:
      --assignee WHO            assign to WHO: me, none, or an email
      --cycle CYCLE             cycle CYCLE (current, next, previous, N, a UUID), or none
      --delegate WHO            delegate to the agent (app user) WHO: its name or email, me, or none
      --description TEXT        the description, Markdown TEXT
      --description-file PATH   read the description from PATH (- for stdin)
      --dry-run                 show what would change; change nothing
      --due-date DATE           the due date, DATE (2026-11-30), or none
      --estimate POINTS         the estimate, POINTS (a whole number), or none
  -h, --help                    help for create
      --id UUID                 the new issue's UUID; required with --yes
      --json-input PATH         read Linear's input object from PATH (- for stdin); flags win
      --label NAME              add label NAME (repeatable)
      --milestone NAME          project milestone NAME, or none to clear; it sets the project
                                when the issue has none
      --parent ISSUE            make it a sub-issue of ISSUE (none: of no issue)
      --priority PRIORITY       PRIORITY: 0-4 or none, urgent, high, medium, low
      --project NAME            project NAME, or none to clear it
      --state NAME              workflow state NAME (see 'linearctl state list')
      --state-type TYPE         the team's first workflow state of TYPE (e.g. started)
      --team KEY                create in team KEY (e.g. ENG)
      --title TEXT              the title, TEXT
      --yes                     apply the change
```

## linearctl issue list

```
List issues, most recently updated first. Filters combine with AND; a repeated
--state or --state-type matches any of its values, a repeated --label all of them;
--any-label matches any of its values, --without-label none of them.
--query searches titles, descriptions and comments, ranked by relevance unless
--sort is given; Linear allows 30 searches a minute. With one --team, it searches
that team, as Linear's team search does.
--team falls back to LINEARCTL_TEAM, then to default-team in config.

Fields: id, identifier, title, priority, priorityLabel, url, createdAt,
updatedAt, dueDate, estimate, state, assignee, delegate, team, project, cycle,
projectMilestone, labels

Usage:
  linearctl issue list [flags]

Examples:
  linearctl issue list --assignee me --state-type started --json
  linearctl issue list --team ENG --label bug --updated-since 7d --fields identifier,title --json
  linearctl issue list --query "login timeout" --limit 10

Flags:
      --any-label NAME         only issues with label NAME (repeatable; any of)
      --assignee WHO           only issues assigned to WHO: me, none, or an email
      --attachment-url URL     only issues with an attachment at URL (e.g. a linked pull request)
      --blocked                only issues blocked by an open issue
      --blocking               only issues that block another
      --completed-since WHEN   only issues completed since WHEN: a date, an RFC 3339 time, 7d or 24h
      --creator WHO            only issues created by WHO: me, none, or an email
      --cursor CURSOR          continue after CURSOR (nextCursor from the previous page)
      --cycle CYCLE            only issues in cycle CYCLE: current, next, previous, a number, a UUID
      --delegate WHO           only issues delegated to the agent WHO (name, email, me, any, none)
      --due-after DATE         only issues due on or after DATE
      --due-before DATE        only issues due on or before DATE (2026-11-30)
      --fields FIELDS          return only these comma-separated FIELDS (see Fields above)
  -h, --help                   help for list
      --id ISSUE               only the issue ISSUE (ENG-123 or a UUID; repeatable); one not
                               found is a problem (exit 3)
      --include-comments       with --query, also match the text of comments
      --label NAME             only issues with label NAME (repeatable; all of)
      --limit N                show at most N items; 0 for all (default 25)
      --milestone NAME         only issues in project milestone NAME (none: in no milestone)
      --priority PRIORITY      only issues of PRIORITY: 0-4 or none, urgent, high, medium, low
                               (repeatable, any of)
      --project NAME           only issues in project NAME (none: in no project)
      --query TEXT             full-text search for TEXT
      --reverse                reverse the order of --sort
      --sort FIELD             FIELD: updated (default), created, priority, due-date, title, state
      --state NAME             only issues in workflow state NAME (repeatable; any of)
      --state-type TYPE        only issues whose state is of TYPE (repeatable): triage, backlog,
                               unstarted, started, completed, canceled, duplicate
      --team KEY               only issues of team KEY (e.g. ENG; repeatable, any of)
      --updated-since WHEN     only issues updated since WHEN: a date, an RFC 3339 time, 7d or 24h
      --view VIEW              only issues in Linear's saved custom view VIEW (a name or its id)
      --without-label NAME     only issues without label NAME (repeatable; none of)
```

## linearctl issue show

```
Show one issue with its description, comments, sub-issues and relations.
ISSUE is an identifier (ENG-123), a UUID, or a linear.app issue URL.
--signed-urls makes file URLs in the result open without the API key for that
many seconds, so a viewer can fetch images directly; signedUrlsExpireAt says until when.
Comments are included (20 by default); give another count as --comments=N.

Fields: id, identifier, title, priority, priorityLabel, url, createdAt,
updatedAt, dueDate, estimate, state, assignee, delegate, team, project, cycle,
projectMilestone, labels, description, branchName, startedAt, completedAt,
canceledAt, archivedAt, creator, parent, children, relations, inverseRelations,
attachments, comments

Usage:
  linearctl issue show ISSUE [flags]

Aliases:
  show, view

Examples:
  linearctl issue show ENG-123
  linearctl issue view ENG-123 --signed-urls 300 --json
  linearctl issue show ENG-123 --comments=0 --fields identifier,title,description --json

Flags:
      --comments N[=20]       include the first N comments (--comments=N); 0 for none (default 20)
      --fields FIELDS         return only these comma-separated FIELDS (see Fields above)
  -h, --help                  help for show
      --signed-urls SECONDS   sign file URLs for SECONDS so they open without the key
```


## linearctl issue update

```
Change an issue's fields. Only fields that differ from the issue as it is are
sent; when none differ, nothing is sent and the result is changed: false.
--label replaces all labels; --add-label and --remove-label adjust them.
State names resolve within the issue's own team.
--if-updated-at TIME refuses (exit 7, conflict) if the issue changed since you
read it.
Changes things: pass --dry-run to preview, --yes to apply.

Usage:
  linearctl issue update ISSUE [flags]

Examples:
  linearctl issue update ENG-123 --state "In Progress" --assignee me --dry-run --json
  linearctl issue update ENG-123 --add-label blocked --priority high --yes

Flags:
      --add-label NAME          add label NAME (repeatable)
      --assignee WHO            assign to WHO: me, none, or an email
      --cycle CYCLE             cycle CYCLE (current, next, previous, N, a UUID), or none
      --delegate WHO            delegate to the agent (app user) WHO: its name or email, me, or none
      --description TEXT        the description, Markdown TEXT
      --description-file PATH   read the description from PATH (- for stdin)
      --dry-run                 show what would change; change nothing
      --due-date DATE           the due date, DATE (2026-11-30), or none
      --estimate POINTS         the estimate, POINTS (a whole number), or none
  -h, --help                    help for update
      --if-updated-at TIME      change it only if its updatedAt is still TIME (else exit 7)
      --json-input PATH         read Linear's input object from PATH (- for stdin); flags win
      --label NAME              set the labels to NAMEs, replacing the rest (repeatable)
      --milestone NAME          project milestone NAME, or none to clear; it sets the project
                                when the issue has none
      --parent ISSUE            make it a sub-issue of ISSUE (none: of no issue)
      --priority PRIORITY       PRIORITY: 0-4 or none, urgent, high, medium, low
      --project NAME            project NAME, or none to clear it
      --remove-label NAME       remove label NAME (repeatable)
      --state NAME              workflow state NAME (see 'linearctl state list')
      --state-type TYPE         the team's first workflow state of TYPE (e.g. started)
      --title TEXT              the title, TEXT
      --yes                     apply the change
```
